problem: The note says the same substitution (z = y^(1−n)) turns a Riccati equation into a linear equation once one particular solution is known. That is false. A Riccati equation y′ = P(x)y² + Q(x)y + R(x) with R ≠ 0 is not made linear by z = y^(1−n); the Bernoulli substitution only handles the case R = 0, n = 2. The standard linearisation needs the known solution y₁ and the shifted reciprocal substitution z = 1/(y − y₁). A student will try z = y^(1−n) on a Riccati equation and get stuck.
fix: Write: "A Riccati equation y′ = P(x)y² + Q(x)y + R(x) is Bernoulli only when R = 0. With R ≠ 0 it becomes linear only after one particular solution y₁ is known, using z = 1/(y − y₁). That shifted-reciprocal substitution is related to, but not the same as, z = y^(1−n)."

problem: The population model uses the letter P for the population, but P(x) already means the coefficient in y′ + P(x)y = Q(x)yⁿ. A student may read dP/dt = rP − aP² as containing the same P as the linear-equation coefficient. The search phrases in Section 3 also repeat word for word the ones given in Beyond.
fix: Use a different symbol for population, e.g. "dN/dt = rN − aN² with N(t) the population, r the growth rate and a the crowding constant; this is Bernoulli with n = 2 in the variable N." Keep the search phrases in one place only.
